key_terms.meaning: A system that is linear (obeys superposition) and time-invariant (a shifted input gives the same shifted output).
For inputs x₁(t) and x₂(t), output to a x₁ + b x₂ is a y₁ + b y₂ for constants a and b.
If x(t) → y(t), then x(t − t₀) → y(t − t₀) for every shift t₀.
Output of an LTI system when the input is the unit impulse δ(t), with zero initial conditions.
Output when the input is the unit step u(t); s(t)=∫_{−∞}^{t} h(τ)dτ.
y(t)=∫_{−∞}^{∞} x(τ)h(t−τ)dτ gives the LTI output for input x(t).
Graphical convolution: reflect h(τ) to h(−τ), shift by t, multiply with x(τ), and integrate over τ.
x(t)*h(t)=h(t)*x(t); order of convolution does not change the result.
(x*h₁)*h₂=x*(h₁*h₂); cascaded LTI systems combine by convolving their impulse responses.
x*(h₁+h₂)=x*h₁+x*h₂; parallel LTI systems add their impulse responses.
x(t)*δ(t)=x(t), so the unit impulse leaves any signal unchanged under convolution.
An LTI system is causal if h(t)=0 for t<0, so output depends only on present and past inputs.
Bounded input gives bounded output; for an LTI system this holds if ∫_{−∞}^{∞}|h(t)|dt<∞.
The area under |h(t)| is finite, written ∫|h(t)|dt<∞; this is the BIBO stability test.
An equation such as Σ a_k d^k y/dt^k = Σ b_k d^k x/dt^k with constant a_k and b_k describes an LTI system.
The part of the output from initial conditions with zero input; it depends on the system characteristic roots.
The part of the output produced by the input with zero initial conditions.
A set of variables such as y(t), dy/dt, … that store the system past and, with the input, determine future behaviour.
A set of first-order equations dx/dt=A x+B u, y=C x+D u for an nth-order system.
The first-order equation dx/dt=A x+B u that updates the state vector x(t).

takeaways: An LTI system is completely described by its impulse response h(t).
Superposition and time invariance let you build the output from shifted scaled impulses.
The step response is the running integral of the impulse response; h(t) is the derivative of s(t).
Convolution is the time-domain rule y=x*h for any LTI system.
Convolution is commutative, associative, distributive, and has δ(t) as identity.
Causality is a support condition on h(t); BIBO stability is an area condition on |h(t)|.
A linear constant-coefficient differential equation is an LTI system; its solution has natural and forced parts.
Any nth-order differential equation can be written as n first-order state equations in normal form.
bank_note: Long answers usually ask for a definition plus derivation, a graphical convolution, a causality or stability test on h(t), or conversion of a differential equation to state form.

bank.q: Define a continuous-time LTI system. Explain the superposition and time-invariance properties, and show why an LTI system is fully characterised by its impulse response.
outline: Definition of linearity: additivity and homogeneity
Definition of time invariance with shifted input
Impulse response as response to δ(t)
Output as convolution of input and h(t)

bank.q: Define impulse response h(t) and step response s(t) of a continuous-time LTI system. Derive the relations s(t)=∫_{−∞}^{t} h(τ)dτ and h(t)=ds(t)/dt.
outline: Input u(t) as integral of δ(t)

bank.q: State the commutative, associative, distributive, and identity properties of continuous-time convolution. Give one system-level meaning of each property.
Define causality and BIBO stability for a continuous-time LTI system. State the necessary and sufficient conditions on h(t) for each.
outline: Causal: output depends only on present and past input
BIBO: bounded input yields bounded output
Sufficiency argument using a bound on x

bank.q: Let x(t)=e^{−2t}u(t) and h(t)=u(t)−u(t−3). Evaluate y(t)=x(t)*h(t) by the convolution integral and give y(t) for all t.
outline: Identify nonzero ranges for τ and t−τ

bank.q: An LTI system has h(t)=e^{−at}u(t), a>0. Find its step response using the convolution integral, and verify the result by differentiating it.
A system is described by dy(t)/dt+3y(t)=2x(t). Find its impulse response h(t) and step response s(t) using time-domain reasoning.
outline: Apply impulse matching or initial condition

bank.q: For h(t)=e^{−4t}u(t), test causality and BIBO stability. Compute the area ∫|h(t)|dt and state the conclusion.
Convert d²y/dt²+5dy/dt+6y=dx/dt+2x into state equations in normal form. Define the state variables clearly.
outline: Handle input derivative by suitable state choice or input u and du/dt
Write matrix form and output equation

bank.q: Compare two LTI systems with h₁(t)=δ(t−1) and h₂(t)=e^{−t}u(t). Discuss causality, BIBO stability, memory, and the output when the input is u(t).
outline: h₁ causal and stable; pure delay
Memory: h₁ has memory (delay), h₂ has infinite memory

bank.q: For the system d²y/dt²+3dy/dt+2y=x(t), discuss natural and forced response. Relate the impulse response to the characteristic roots.
outline: Initial conditions and zero-input or zero-state parts

bank.q: Explain the graphical evaluation of the convolution integral. Use x(t)=u(t)−u(t−2) and h(t)=u(t)−u(t−1) to obtain y(t), and comment on the duration and shape.
outline: Result is trapezoid or triangle shape
Duration equals sum of input durations

bank.q: A student claims: 'Every causal LTI system is BIBO stable.' Evaluate the claim. Either prove it or give a counterexample using h(t), and state the correct relation between causality and stability.

glossary.def: A system that is both linear and time-invariant.
The property that a system obeys superposition: scaling and adding inputs scales and adds outputs.
Output to a combination of inputs equals the same combination of individual outputs.
Output to x₁+x₂ equals output to x₁ plus output to x₂.
Output to a x(t) equals a times output to x(t) for any constant a.
A time shift in the input produces the same time shift in the output.
A signal that is zero except at t=0, has unit area, and satisfies ∫δ(t)dt=1.
A signal equal to 1 for t≥0 and 0 for t<0.
The output of an LTI system to input δ(t) with zero initial conditions.
The output of an LTI system to input u(t) with zero initial conditions.
The operation y(t)=∫x(τ)h(t−τ)dτ that gives the output of an LTI system.
Order of the two signals in convolution can be exchanged without changing the result.
Grouping of three convolved signals can be changed without changing the result.
Convolution distributes over addition of impulse responses.
A system property where the output at time t depends only on inputs up to time t.
Every bounded input produces a bounded output.
A signal h(t) with finite area under its absolute value, ∫|h(t)|dt<∞.
An equation relating an output and its derivatives to an input and its derivatives.
A differential equation whose coefficients are constants and whose terms are linear in y, x, and derivatives.
The zero-input part of the output, fixed by initial conditions and system roots.
The zero-state part of the output, produced by the input.
The polynomial equation obtained by setting the homogeneous part of a differential equation to zero.
A variable in a minimal set that, with the input, determines the future of the system.
A column vector collecting all state variables of a system.
A first-order vector equation dx/dt=Ax+Bu plus output equation y=Cx+Du.
The equation dx/dt=Ax+Bu that updates the state vector.
